Hi Anna — thanks for the clear note and the forecast. Quick summary up front, then two concrete options below:

High-level: We support both marginal and blended approaches, plus a hybrid that we recommend for customers with spiky usage. The main trade-offs are predictability (blended) vs. economic efficiency on bursts (marginal). Clawbacks/true-ups are negotiable but typically handled as monthly true-ups with a multi-month recovery window.

Option A — Pure marginal ladder (simpler to bill)
- Example breakpoints: 0–100M tokens @ $0.00038, 100M–500M @ $0.00031, 500M+ @ $0.00024
- Billing: tokens priced at their marginal band in each billing period (no retroactive averaging)
- Pros: simple, predictable for us; customers with bursty months only pay for what they use that month
- Cons: large month-to-month variability in effective spend for you

Option B — Hybrid (recommended for Veritas)
- Same band breakpoints, but we apply a blended credit at the end of each month if your trailing quarterly usage meets the committed tiers. That gives you downside protection during an early ramp and preserves the marginal economics during sustained volume.
- Example mechanics: monthly invoice uses marginal pricing; if quarter-end trailing 3-month usage exceeds threshold for a higher band, we apply a credit to retroactively blend the prior months to the higher effective rate (so you get some of the upside discount without large one-time refunds).

Clawback suggestions
- Typical: 3–6 month lookback with pro-rata recapture of credits if annual committed volume is not met. For pilots we can shorten to 1–3 months.
- We also include an early-termination true-up: unused committed tokens are billed at the base marginal rates or offset by any advance credits received.

Hi Anna — quick recap and the mechanics we recommend based on your forecast and procurement's ask. Draft SOW attached.

Headline structure (proposal):
- Commit: Annual committed tokens = 1.2B tokens (this is illustrative; we'll finalize after you confirm target)
- Breakpoints and published marginal rates (monthly billing uses marginal band pricing):
  • Band A: 0 — 100,000,000 tokens @ $0.00039/token
  • Band B: 100,000,001 — 400,000,000 tokens @ $0.00029/token
  • Band C: 400,000,001+ tokens @ $0.00021/token
- Monthly billing: each token billed at the marginal band price for that month
- Blended credit: At the end of each calendar month Redwood calculates trailing 3-month usage. If the trailing 3-month usage places you in a higher band than invoiced months, Redwood will apply a credit to retroactively reduce invoices to a blended effective rate for that trailing period.
- Credit recovery / clawback: Any credits issued under the blended-credit mechanism are recoverable against future invoices for a period of four months from issuance if the annual committed tokens are not met; after four months, remaining credits are forfeited.
- Early termination: standard true-up at the marginal band rates for any remaining committed tokens; pre-paid credits applied first.

Example (illustrative):
- Jan usage: 60M tokens (billed at Band A rates)
- Feb usage: 140M tokens (60M @ A + 80M @ B)
- Mar usage: 30M tokens
- Trailing 3-month = 230M -> places the trailing window in Band B average; we apply a blended credit to partially refund the incremental overage relative to Band B effective rate.

Next steps
- If you confirm 1) committed tokens target and 2) that procurement is okay with a 4-month recovery window, I'll share an updated Draft-SOW (attached) for redline by legal. We can take a short 30-minute call if procurement prefers to talk through the example.
